newsitem.title: FINLAND: EMU FX CONVERSION PRINCIPLES OPEN - FINNISH OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: EMU FX CONVERSION PRINCIPLES OPEN - FINNISH OFFICIAL.

text.p: A senior official at the Finnish finance ministry said on Friday it was premature to talk about at what level the markka may be irrevocably fixed to the euro since even the conversion principles had not been agreed.

Martti Hetemaki, head of the economics department, told Reuters by telephone that the central parity rate in Europe's exchange rate mechanism was "only one method" for the conversion prior to the start of the launch of Europe's single currency.
On Tuesday, Rauno Niinimaki, head of the finance ministry's EMU project, was quoted as saying that the markka's conversion rate was unlikely to differ much from its ERM central parity.

The markka briefly weakened to over 3.00 per German mark on his remarks, edging closer to the DEM/FIM 3.04 ERM midpoint, but soon strengthened back to its recent trading range around 2.99 markka per mark.
Hetemaki said Niinimaki's conclusion was apparently "based on the interpretation of a lot of insufficient and generally worded texts".
"At this stage, when even the principles for the conversion have not been agreed, it is too early to talk about the exchange rate's conversion level," he said.

Hetemaki noted that Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer had recently expressed his hope that European Union finance ministers and central bank governors should agree in September this year how the final exchange rates will be fixed.
He declined comment when asked what kind of conversion principles Finland might be looking for. He also declined to comment on what conversion rate would be appropriate.
The third stage of European economic and monetary union (EMU) is scheduled to begin in January 1999.
